Exercise A

A Country of Many Cultures

Read the text about Canada. Choose the correct word for each gap.

Before you read — optional, not marked
This is just to get you thinking — you can leave it empty and it does not count towards your score.
Reading Text

Canada is often called one of the most multicultural countries in the world. Two 1 languages, English and French, are spoken across the country, and more than 200 other languages are used at home by immigrant families.

Every year, hundreds of thousands of new 2 arrive in Canada from all over the world, bringing their own food, music and traditions with them.

Toronto, the country's largest city, is one of the most 3 cities on Earth — more than half of its population was born outside Canada.

The government actively supports multiculturalism: it was made official policy in 1971, and it is protected by law today. Schools are encouraged to celebrate different cultural 4 throughout the year.

Of course, Canada's history also includes the 5 peoples who lived there long before any settlers arrived, and their cultures remain an important part of the country today.

For many Canadians, this mix of cultures is a source of national 6.

Exercise B

Passive Voice: Simple Present

am / is / are + past participle. English and French are spoken in Canada.

Complete the Sentence

1. English and French in Canada.

2. Maple syrup mostly in Quebec.

3. Many festivals across the country every year.

4. Ice hockey in almost every Canadian town.

5. New immigrants in most Canadian communities.

6. Multiculturalism by Canadian law.

7. Diversity as a national strength.

8. Different languages at home by many families.

Exercise C

Passive Voice: Simple Past

was / were + past participle. Multiculturalism was made official policy in 1971.

Complete the Sentence

1. Multiculturalism official policy in 1971.

2. Canada as a country in 1867.

3. Thousands of new immigrants last year alone.

4. The festival by local volunteers.

5. The law by the Canadian parliament.

6. Traditional foods by every family at the street party.

7. The documentary in three different provinces.

8. The new citizens to a special ceremony.

Exercise D

Writing: My Country or City

Write 6–8 sentences about your own country, region or city. Use at least three passive sentences — a mix of simple present and simple past.

Think about these questions

• What languages are spoken where you live?

• What is your region famous for?

• What festivals are celebrated there?

• What important event happened there in the past?

You can use these: ... is spoken ... is known for ... ... is celebrated every year ... was founded in ... ... was built in ...
Your text
Aim for 6–8 sentences with three passive sentences (present and past).
